canonical_question: What role does the B2 phase play in the overall mechanical integrity of the HEA after selective dissolution in the molten salt?

question_variants.question: What role does the B2 phase play in the overall mechanical integrity of the HEA after selective dissolution in the molten salt?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text identifies that the B2 phase undergoes selective dissolution and that the FCC phase acts as a barrier, but it does not explicitly quantify the specific role of the B2 phase in the 'overall mechanical integrity' (e.g., load bearing vs. sacrificial) after the dissolution event.

answers.answer: The document notes the selective dissolution of the B2 phase and the role of the FCC-L12 phase as a barrier, but does not provide a specific assessment of the resulting mechanical integrity of the bulk alloy after this dissolution.
answers.boundary_limitation: Mechanical properties not detailed post-corrosion in this context
evidence_spans: Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205).
The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.
